data.text: Storybook is an open-source tool for developing UI components in isolation. It supports addons for documentation, accessibility, and testing.

data.title: Storybook story

data.text: A story renders one component in one state. Collectively, stories become a catalogue that designers, reviewers, and testers can browse without running the app. Each story controls props through `args`, which the Storybook UI exposes as editable controls.

data.title: Stories with args and controls

data.text: A `play` function drives the component inside Storybook, so an interaction can be asserted in the same place the story lives. Stories can also be reused as the fixture for unit tests, which means the same example is exercised in the catalogue and in CI.

data.title: A play function asserts behavior
Storybook is documentation plus a test surface
data.text: The reason teams adopt it is that it forces a component to be renderable in isolation, which exposes hidden global coupling. The bonus is that the stories can run as visual regression tests and interaction tests. Say that the primary value is the catalogue and that testing is a second benefit, not the other way round.

terms.definition: A single state of a component.
